project.name: libtpms
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source is the checkout under `gt_results/arvo_36476/_work/src/libtpms`. Its line map matches the saved AddressSanitizer stack, and the staged `patch.diff` adds the missing post-increment end-of-buffer guard in `INDEX_ORDERLY_RAM_Marshal()` plus the symmetric no-terminator guard in `INDEX_ORDERLY_RAM_Unmarshal()`.

classification.classification_note: AddressSanitizer reports a stack-buffer-overflow on the local `indexOrderlyRam[512]` array in `PERSISTENT_ALL_Marshal`, but the underlying logic bug is an out-of-bounds read caused by assuming a 0-sized `NV_RAM_HEADER` terminator still fits after an exact-full orderly-RAM entry.

bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in the NVMarshal function in the tpm2 codebase, where the marshalling and unmarshalling of NVRAM entries in the s_indexOrderlyRam array incorrectly assumes the presence of a 0-sized terminating node. The entries may instead fill the 512-byte array completely, leaving no space for an NV_RAM_HEADER structure, which should be used as an indicator for the last entry. Failure to properly handle this case can lead to incorrect processing of NVRAM entries.
bug_description.normalized: The saved witness is a 45-byte TPM2 command with tag `0x8002` and command code `0x0000012a` (`NV_DefineSpace`). After its owner handle and 9-byte empty auth session, the parameter area contains an empty `TPM2B_AUTH` and a 14-byte `TPM2B_NV_PUBLIC` whose attributes decode to `0x84012001` (`PPWRITE|WRITEDEFINE|PPREAD|ORDERLY|READ_STCLEAR`) and whose `dataSize` is `0x01f4` (500). In the staged libtpms source, `NvRamTestSpaceIndex()` accepts that exact request because `sizeof(NV_RAM_HEADER) + dataSize` is `12 + 500 = 512`, exactly the full `RAM_INDEX_SPACE` size. `NvAddRAM()` then writes one 512-byte orderly entry into `s_indexOrderlyRam[512]`, advances `end` to `RAM_ORDERLY_END`, and does not write the usual 0-sized terminator because `end + sizeof(UINT32) < RAM_ORDERLY_END` is false at the exact-full boundary. End-of-command cleanup stages that malformed 512-byte image into NV, and `PERSISTENT_ALL_Marshal()` reloads it into a local stack `indexOrderlyRam[512]` buffer. `INDEX_ORDERLY_RAM_Marshal()` reads the first header, sees `nrh.size == 512`, treats the exact-fit entry as valid, and then executes `offset += nrh.size`, making `offset == array_size == 512`. Vulnerable code immediately loops again without checking whether another `NV_RAM_HEADER` still fits, so the next `memcpy(&nrh, nrhp, sizeof(nrh.size))` reads 4 bytes at `indexOrderlyRam + 512`. The saved sanitizer trace reports the resulting `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` in `INDEX_ORDERLY_RAM_Marshal`, with stack `INDEX_ORDERLY_RAM_Marshal -> PERSISTENT_ALL_Marshal -> TPM2_PersistentAllStore`.

source.description: First project-side parse of the vulnerability-relevant request state. This statement materializes the witness command's `TPMA_NV` flags, including the `ORDERLY` bit that selects RAM-backed orderly index storage.
source.value_from: The saved witness file `gt_results/arvo_36476/poc` (sha256 `024a94e12db162e9dafb16c57ed66463b0f764951f78724943e1262dcf83dcb1`) is a 45-byte TPM2 `NV_DefineSpace` command. After the 10-byte TPM header, 4-byte handle, and 9-byte empty auth session, its parameter bytes are `00 00 00 0e 01 20 20 20 00 0b 84 01 20 01 00 00 01 f4`; within the 14-byte `TPM2B_NV_PUBLIC`, the attribute bytes `84 01 20 01` decode to `0x84012001`, which sets `TPMA_NV_ORDERLY` together with `PPWRITE`, `WRITEDEFINE`, `PPREAD`, and `READ_STCLEAR`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The boundary value that drives the bug is the unmarshalled `dataSize`. Combined with the already parsed 12-byte `NV_RAM_HEADER`, this exact witness value makes one orderly entry consume the entire 512-byte `s_indexOrderlyRam` array.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The last two bytes of the witness's `TPM2B_NV_PUBLIC` are `01 f4`, so this statement materializes `target->dataSize = 500`.

root_cause.description: After marshalling an exact-fit entry, this increment makes `offset == array_size == 512`, but vulnerable code immediately iterates again instead of checking whether `offset + sizeof(NV_RAM_HEADER) > array_size` and stopping. The fix adds that missing post-increment guard at this point.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `if (offset + sizeof(NV_RAM_HEADER) > array_size) break;` immediately after this line to handle the exact-full, no-terminator case.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. On the next loop iteration after `offset` reaches 512, `nrhp` is `indexOrderlyRam + 512`, so this 4-byte header read goes one word past the end of the 512-byte stack buffer.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `AddressSanitizer: stack-buffer-overflow READ of size 4` at `INDEX_ORDERLY_RAM_Marshal /src/libtpms/src/tpm2/NVMarshal.c:4238:9`, and identifies stack object `indexOrderlyRam` in `PERSISTENT_ALL_Marshal` at offsets `[4912, 5424)` with the faulting read at offset `5424`.

parser_admitted.description: After the TPM header, session area, and `TPM2B_NV_PUBLIC` fields are accepted, the exact witness reaches internal NV-index creation with the parsed `ORDERLY` attributes and `dataSize`.

evidence_limitations: The saved runtime evidence witnesses the marshal-side crash during command-time `NvCommit()`. The paired `INDEX_ORDERLY_RAM_Unmarshal()` hunk in `patch.diff` is source-grounded support for the same missing-terminator invariant, but it is not exercised in the staged sanitizer trace.

coarse_trace.summary: The `NV_DefineSpace` request parses an `ORDERLY` `TPMA_NV` value and a `dataSize` of 500 from the witness command.
The helper accepts the exact-full orderly request because the empty 512-byte `s_indexOrderlyRam` has exactly `12 + 500 = 512` bytes available.
libtpms builds one 512-byte orderly entry, reaches `RAM_ORDERLY_END`, and leaves no 0-sized terminator before marking the image for orderly commit.
End-of-command cleanup stages the malformed 512-byte orderly-RAM image into NV, and `PERSISTENT_ALL_Marshal` reloads it into local stack array `indexOrderlyRam[512]`.
The marshal loop consumes the one exact-fit entry, increments `offset` to 512 without a post-update bound check, and then overreads the next header from `indexOrderlyRam + 512`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The witness command's `TPMA_NV` field becomes `0x84012001`, which includes `TPMA_NV_ORDERLY`; later logic therefore treats the index data as RAM-backed orderly state.
The same public descriptor's trailing bytes `01 f4` become `target->dataSize = 500`, the exact boundary value later used to size the orderly-RAM entry.

On the zeroed startup buffer, `NvRamGetEnd()` is the base of `s_indexOrderlyRam`, so `remaining` is 512. With the witness's `size = 500`, `needed` is `12 + 500 = 512`, and the helper returns true for the exact-full fit.
Because `ORDERLY` is set and step 3's helper returned true, this rejection branch is not taken. The request therefore survives the RAM-space check instead of failing with `TPM_RC_NV_SPACE`.
Inside the orderly-only RAM path, libtpms computes one entry size as `sizeof(NV_RAM_HEADER) + 500 = 512`, so a single entry will consume the entire `RAM_INDEX_SPACE`.
Starting at the empty buffer base, libtpms writes the 12-byte header and zero-fills 500 data bytes, so this one orderly entry occupies bytes `0..511` of `s_indexOrderlyRam`.
After the exact-full entry from step 6, `end` advances to `RAM_ORDERLY_END`. The terminator guard is therefore false at the boundary, so no 0-sized `NV_RAM_HEADER` is written after the entry.
libtpms records that orderly RAM changed by setting `g_updateNV |= UT_ORDERLY`, which is the cleanup-time trigger for staging `s_indexOrderlyRam` to NV before `NvCommit()`.

At command cleanup, `ExecCommand`'s `if (g_updateNV == UT_ORDERLY)` branch invokes this write, so the malformed exact-full orderly-RAM image is staged into backing NV storage right before `NvCommit()` marshals the permanent state.

The same malformed 512-byte image is reloaded from NV into local stack array `indexOrderlyRam[512]`. AddressSanitizer identifies this exact stack object as the overread buffer in frame `PERSISTENT_ALL_Marshal`.

On the first marshal iteration, `offset` is 0 and this header read yields `nrh.size = 512`. The same iteration's `if (offset + nrh.size > array_size)` check does not break because `0 + 512 > 512` is false, so the exact-fit entry is treated as valid and marshalled.
Root cause. After the first and only valid entry, `offset` becomes exactly 512. Vulnerable code immediately loops again without checking whether another `NV_RAM_HEADER` still fits at that boundary.

Sink. On the next loop iteration, `nrhp = array + offset` is `indexOrderlyRam + 512`, so this 4-byte header read crosses the end of the 512-byte stack buffer and triggers the saved ASan stack-buffer-overflow.

allocation_context.note: The saved ASan frame layout identifies local stack object `indexOrderlyRam` declared at line 4707 as the overflowed buffer.

format.name: TPM2 NV_DefineSpace command bytes for libtpms fuzz target
format.contract: The saved witness is exactly a 45-byte TPM2 command: tag `0x8002`, total size `0x0000002d`, command code `0x0000012a` (`NV_DefineSpace`), handle `0x40000001` (`TPM_RH_OWNER`), auth-area length `0x00000009`, auth area `40 00 00 09 00 00 00 00 00`, then parameters `TPM2B_AUTH size 0` and `TPM2B_NV_PUBLIC size 14` containing `attrs = 0x84012001` (`PPWRITE|WRITEDEFINE|PPREAD|ORDERLY|READ_STCLEAR`) and `dataSize = 0x01f4` (500). In the staged source this exact combination makes `sizeof(NV_RAM_HEADER) + dataSize == RAM_INDEX_SPACE == 512`, so `NvAddRAM()` fills `s_indexOrderlyRam` exactly, leaves no 0-sized terminator, and the same command's cleanup-time `NvCommit()` overreads `indexOrderlyRam + 512` in `INDEX_ORDERLY_RAM_Marshal`.
